sup:70620.text:
Dear customer,

Thank you for your enquiry. Please find our Angebot below. We are pleased to present our current offer for your requirements, maintaining our commitment to supporting your business with top-quality service and our extensive product range.

For this offer, we quote a price of €4.96 per unit, with a Zahlungsziel 30 days net and a contract term of 12 months. Please note that this offer remains valid for 30 days.

To provide some background on our pricing calculations, LCI-C rose 2.7 % in twelve months and is 10 % of our cost. Furthermore, PPI-C2815 rose 0.8 % in twelve months and is 65 % of our cost.

Mit freundlichen Grüßen
Florian Gruber
Inside Sales, Wälzlager-Zentrum Süd GmbH

move.subject: Re: Quote from Wälzlager-Zentrum Süd GmbH: Renewal of the ball bearing 6306 agreement
move.body:
Dear Sir or Madam,

Thank you for your offer and for explaining your position.
Thank you for your note on renewing our framework agreement. We value the long cooperation and, as you asked, we are sharing our expected volumes for the bearing, which show steady and rising demand. We propose a multi-year agreement with firm volumes, which gives you planning security and less handling effort, at today's price basis. We would also gladly take up the owner's offer to walk through the calculation together.

Our data shows a different picture on some points:
Our demand forecast for this part has risen 4.2% (fc:360020@2026-09).
Our latest orders for this part were all at EUR 4.39 per unit (po:4500014467-10, po:4500014389-10, po:4500014329-10).
Your rolling scorecard shows on-time delivery of 85.0% (sc:70620@2026Q3).

Please find our proposal below.

We look forward to your reply.

Kind regards
Purchasing
Hollerau Pumpenwerke GmbH

move.text:
Dear customer,

We have reviewed your offer and can adjust our Angebot as follows. We checked the delivery record data you cited; it holds, but it does not change our calculation. We checked the price history data you cited; it holds, but it does not change our calculation. We checked the volume change data you cited; it holds, but it does not change our calculation. That does not change our position. Thank you for your proposal and the shared volume forecasts.

Our offer is a price of €4.94 per unit, Zahlungsziel 90 days net, a contract term of 24 months. We are agreeable to a 24-month contract to provide mutual planning security, but we must maintain our standard 30-day payment terms. Alternatively, with Zahlungsziel 30 days net: a price of €4.88 per unit, Zahlungsziel 30 days net, a contract term of 24 months.

Our standard terms apply to everything the quote does not state; see attached. Our general terms and conditions apply; the quote lists our standard terms. Our price follows our main cost drivers: PPI-C2815, LCI-C. We are happy to discuss this in a call; until then our offer stands. Our offer stays valid for 30 days.

Mit freundlichen Grüßen
Florian Gruber
Inside Sales, Wälzlager-Zentrum Süd GmbH

Thank you for your revised proposal. We have carefully reviewed your offer, but we are unable to accommodate further price reductions for these terms. As a trusted partner, we always strive to provide you with the best service and top-quality components from our extensive range, but our price follows our main cost drivers: PPI-C2815, LCI-C.

Mit freundlichen Grüßen
Florian Gruber

backoffice.text: Read the buyer's e-mail: … term sheet and … cited facts to check; we answer with our offer.
Read the buyer's e-mail: … term sheet and … cited fact to check; we answer with our offer.
Read the buyer's e-mail: … term sheet; we answer with our final offer.

key_points: Routine renewal of one bearing, two years, need fixed; fallback second-source quote is dearer than the current price, so our walk-away is weak and must stay in the background.
Supplier is sound, sees us as small and wants volume and multi-year deals: offer twenty-four months as the main trade for a price hold.
Payment is now at our standard sixty days; the supplier has no cash need, so keep sixty and do not spend price on shorter payment.
Lead with our rising forecast and the price history; keep the delivery shortfall and quality notifications as fresh facts for later rounds, framed as joint improvement.
Never cite the rival's order price, the rival quote or market news on copper and steel; rebut steel claims with the bearing producer price index if they raise it.
Accept a declared final offer if it beats the fallback.
plan.stance_why: Routine goal with a sound supplier that can afford to drop us and a fallback quote above the current price, so a hard anchor risks losing it. Its cost drivers justify little, though, and past renewals settled far below the ask, so a moderate anchor with a length trade fits.

levers.why: Answers its volume request with a checkable rising forecast; volume is its main currency.

argument.sentence: Our demand forecast for this part has risen 4.2% (fc:360020@2026-09).
argument.note: Snapshot 2026-09: 28600 for the next 12 months against 27440 ordered in the last 12 months (requested dates); shared with suppliers: True. More volume is worth more to it.

levers.why: Establishes the current price as the verified basis for the renewal.

argument.sentence: Our latest orders for this part were all at EUR 4.39 per unit (po:4500014467-10, po:4500014389-10, po:4500014329-10).
argument.note: What we pay now: [4.39, 4.39, 4.39] per unit (2026-08-25 to 2026-09-28); anchors any increase.

levers.why: Context showing that past asks settled far lower; frame it gently to set realistic expectations.

argument.note: 3 renewals: asked +5.1% on average, settled +2.1% (gap 2.9 pp); last 2025-12-05: asked +5.7%, settled +2.3%. It usually settles well below its ask.

levers.why: A fresh, checkable fact for a later round: on-time delivery is below target, framed as something to fix together.

argument.sentence: Your rolling scorecard shows on-time delivery of 85.0% (sc:70620@2026Q3).
argument.note: Rolling 12 months to 2026-09-30: 85.0% on time against the requested date (86.2% against its own confirmed date); target 95%; peers' median 84.6%; class A green. A year earlier 88.9%.

levers.why: A further fresh fact: the notifications on this part show much higher ppm than the scorecard, which argues against paying more for a weaker service.

argument.sentence: Our recent quality notifications on this part average 1821 ppm (qn:20004968, qn:20004869, qn:20004857, qn:20004762, qn:20004732, qn:20004711).
argument.note: 6 supplier-caused complaints on this part in the last 12 months (leakage at test, missing marking, porosity, wrong material certificate); EUR 450 recharged; 0 without a closed 8D. Per-lot ppm is jumpy (KNOWN_ISSUES 10): the scorecard's rolling ppm is the fairer figure.

levers.why: Price history filler showing increases already taken.

argument.sentence: Our earliest orders on record for this part were all at EUR 4.12 per unit (po:4500010043-10, po:4500010108-10, po:4500010171-10).
argument.note: Earliest orders [4.12, 4.12, 4.12] per unit (2023-10-09 to 2023-11-08); now +6.6% against them - its price has not fallen since.

levers.why: Prices are fixed per calendar year, so any change starts only at year start.

argument.sentence: Our framework agreement fixes prices for each calendar year.
argument.note: ctr:4600070620#3.1 (price): Prices as per the price annex, fixed for each calendar year. Changes require written notice of at least 60 days before the end of the calendar year.

trades.why: It says only multi-year agreements move prices; twenty-four months captures that value at no cost to us, since our need spans two years.
Keeps our standard sixty days, which the framework already sets; the supplier has no cash need, so do not trade it away.

sup:70620.opening_paragraph: Thank you for your note on renewing our framework agreement. We value the long cooperation and, as you asked, we are sharing our expected volumes for the bearing, which show steady and rising demand. We propose a multi-year agreement with firm volumes, which gives you planning security and less handling effort, at today's price basis. We would also gladly take up the owner's offer to walk through the calculation together.
watch_for: Steel or labour cost claims: rebut with the bearing producer price index and the small labour share; never cite general market news.
A suggestion to buy from the second source instead: do not escalate, and restate the volume offer.
Pressure toward list pricing or a lapse of the agreement: answer promptly and keep a sheet on the table.
A declared final offer: compare it with the fallback and accept if better.
A request for faster payment: decline politely and commit to paying on time.
A hold after the first counter: stop shrinking steps and close near its number.

risks: The fallback quote is above the current price, so the supplier can call any switching hint; never imply one.
The supplier deprioritises us and may let the agreement lapse to list prices if rounds go silent or pressure is high.
Pushing this part too hard may spill over to the single-source bearing it also supplies.
Evidence on its true cost is thin, with no should-cost, so we rely on index and history arguments.
Pushing past a final offer leads to withdrawal.
